output.name: Halvúra

anatomy.part: right tip of the flame (the brightest star, the knife-spark)
the notch between the two flame tongues
the hot heart of the fire, inside the inner core
right rim of the clay bowl

output.myth: On the longest night, when the sun is a thin thread, the old women build the Long Night Fire. My grandmother says it was lit from one spark that fell off Aun's knife the day he cut the string. He was sorry, and the spark was all he could carry home. He gave it to Hesk, who set it in a clay bowl and kept it turning so the wind could not take it. Tavo came down laughing and blew on it, and it only grew. Every hearth on the islands takes a coal from that fire before the year turns. Ennu says you must never let it out, even when you are tired. The bowl is still up there, burning, and the Gulls carry its heat down to us every winter, passed hand to hand like a cup.
output.verse:
A spark off Aun's knife,
the Gulls carry its warmth down,
hand to hand till dawn.
